market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox’s crushing 2022 general-election loss (32 points) and the Maryland GOP’s likely desire to return to the moderate, winning playbook of Larry Hogan make him a vulnerable primary incumbent. Although he retains a Trump-aligned base and could receive another endorsement, primary voters may prioritize electability, and credible challengers could emerge. I estimate his true chance of repeating as the nominee at ~45%, well below the market’s 57.5% implied probability.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 general election to Wes Moore by 32 percentage points, a historic margin for a Maryland GOP nominee.
No major challenger has yet announced, but the Maryland Republican establishment is expected to recruit a moderate candidate similar to Larry Hogan’s style.
Trump’s renewed presidential endorsement would boost Cox, but primary turnout dynamics and voter sentiment after the 2022 debacle remain uncertain.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of Maryland GOP primary dynamics
